{"goal": "Elementary finite-sum and trigonometric-correlation verification: seek a genuinely independent proof of the sharp cyclic inequality, validate equality and constants by exact finite calculations, and audit exceptional cases without disguising spectral arguments as elementary independence.", "kind": "leaf", "node_id": "n-3790f8503746", "research_state": "{"evidence": "Write \u03bb\u2082=4sin\u00b2\u03b8 and \u03b3=\u03bb\u2082\u2212\u03bb\u2081=\u03bb\u2081(1+2cos\u03b8)>0 for N\u22654. All cyclic indices are modulo N; every norm is the unnormalized Euclidean norm.\n\nPROJECTION. The finite identity (1\u2212q)\u2211_{j=0}^{N\u22121}q\u02b2=1\u2212q\u1d3a gives \u2211e^{ik\u03b8j}=0 whenever N does not divide k. Consequently cosine and sine at frequency \u03b8 have zero means, squared norms N/2, and inner product zero. Thus v=P_Nx has v_j=a cos(\u03b8j)+b sin(\u03b8j), where a=(2/N)\u2211_l x_l cos(\u03b8l) and b=(2/N)\u2211_l x_l sin(\u03b8l). Set z=x\u2212v. Then z is perpendicular to V_N, has zero mean, and M(x\u2212u)=M(z)+M(v\u2212u) for every u\u2208V_N. Hence dist(x,V_N)\u00b2=M(z). Cyclic summation by parts gives \u2211\u0394v_j \u0394z_j=\u2211(2v_j\u2212v_{j\u22121}\u2212v_{j+1})z_j=\u03bb\u2081\u2211v_jz_j. The same recurrence gives E(v)=\u03bb\u2081M(v), so expansion proves D(x)=D(z).\n\nREFLECTION REDUCTION. For each r=0,...,N\u22121 set y_j=z_j\u2212z_{r\u2212j} and s_j=sin(\u03b8(j\u2212r/2)). Direct expansion gives \u2211_r M(y)=2NM(z), \u2211_r D(y)=2ND(z), and \u2211_r y_j=Nz_j. Moreover, \u2211_j y_js_j=2\u2211_j z_js_j=0. At sine zeros, reflection fixes the vertex, so y_j=0. With t_j=y_j/s_j elsewhere and t_j=0 at these zeros, expansion using s_{j\u22121}+s_{j+1}=2cos\u03b8 s_j gives D(y)=\u2211_j s_js_{j+1}(t_{j+1}\u2212t_j)\u00b2. A sign-changing edge has reflected endpoints: its intervening sine zero lies at its half-integer midpoint. Its ratios are therefore equal, so every negative-weight term vanishes.\n\nList the positive-sine vertices consecutively along a lifted cyclic arc. Their angles are h\u2081,...,h_m\u2208(0,\u03c0), with spacing \u03b8. Put s_i=sin h_i, w_i=s_i\u00b2, a_i=s_i s_{i+1}, and retain t_i=y_i/s_i on this arc. Reflection duplicates its mass and positive-edge energy. Therefore, defining S=\u2211_{i=1}^m w_it_i\u00b2 and T=\u2211_{i=1}^{m\u22121}a_i(t_{i+1}\u2212t_i)\u00b2, we have M(y)=2S, D(y)=2T, and \u2211_{i=1}^m w_it_i=0. If m=1, the last identity forces y=0.\n\nNEW SHARP WEIGHTED CERTIFICATE. Assume m\u22652. Set \u03c6_i=cos h_i and p_i=a_i(\u03c6_i\u2212\u03c6_{i+1})>0 for 1\u2264i<m, with p\u2080=p_m=0. At an omitted boundary edge, either the neighboring sine is zero, or the two angles are \u00b1\u03b8/2 or \u03c0\u00b1\u03b8/2 and have equal cosines. Thus its flux really is zero, covering odd and even N without discarded boundary terms.\n\nDefine F_i=\u2211_{k=1}^i w_kt_k, so F\u2080=F_m=0, and J=\u2211_{i=1}^{m\u22121}F_i\u00b2/a_i. Since S=\u2211_{i=1}^m(F_i\u2212F_{i\u22121})\u00b2/w_i, direct expansion yields the dual factorization\nK:=S\u2212\u03b3J=\u2211_{i=1}^{m\u22122}(p_ip_{i+1}/w_{i+1})(F_i/p_i\u2212F_{i+1}/p_{i+1})\u00b2\u22650.\nTo check every diagonal coefficient, use\n(p_i\u2212p_{i\u22121})/w_i\u2212(p_{i+1}\u2212p_i)/w_{i+1}=\u03b3p_i/a_i.\nThe cross coefficients on both sides are \u22122F_iF_{i+1}/w_{i+1}. Finally, finite summation by parts gives \u2211_{i=1}^{m\u22121}F_i(t_{i+1}\u2212t_i)=\u2212S. Expanding squares now proves the explicit strengthened certificate\nT\u2212\u03b3S=\u2211_{i=1}^{m\u22121}a_i(t_{i+1}\u2212t_i+\u03b3F_i/a_i)\u00b2+\u03b3K\u22650.\nAveraging over reflections gives D(z)\u2212\u03b3M(z)=N\u207b\u00b9\u2211_r(T_r\u2212\u03b3S_r)\u22650, proving the requested estimate.\n\nCOMPLETE EQUALITY. If T\u2212\u03b3S=0, then K=0. Its positive coefficients force F_i=\u03bap_i; for m=2 this proportionality is automatic because there is only one coordinate. Hence t_i=(F_i\u2212F_{i\u22121})/w_i=\u03ba\u03b3 cos h_i. Reflection and the zero vertices show that y_j is proportional to sin(2\u03b8(j\u2212r/2)). The singleton case gives y=0 and satisfies the same conclusion. Equality after averaging forces this conclusion for every r. Since z_j=N\u207b\u00b9\u2211_r y_j, it follows that z belongs to W_N=span_R{cos(2\u03b8j),sin(2\u03b8j)}. This excludes all additional equality cases.\n\nSHARPNESS AND SMALL N. For N\u22654, finite geometric sums at frequencies 1,2,3 show W_N is perpendicular to constants and V_N. For N\u22655, its cosine and sine have squared norms N/2 and inner product zero. At N=4, its sine vanishes and its cosine is (\u22121)^j, with squared norm 4. For every w\u2208W_N, the direct recurrence 2w_j\u2212w_{j\u22121}\u2212w_{j+1}=\u03bb\u2082w_j and summation by parts give E(w)=\u03bb\u2082M(w), hence D(w)=\u03b3M(w). A nonzero cosine therefore proves optimality, and stability equality is exactly x=v+w with v\u2208V_N and w\u2208W_N. Original Poincare equality instead requires w=0.\n\nFor N=4, \u03b3=2 and the orthogonal spaces V_4 and W_4 have dimensions 2 and 1, exhausting the mean-zero space. Thus D(x)=2dist(x,V_4)\u00b2 for every admissible x; the alternating vector has M=4 and E=16. For N=5, \u03b3=\u221a5 and both harmonic spaces have dimension 2, exhausting the four-dimensional mean-zero space; therefore D(x)=\u221a5dist(x,V_5)\u00b2 identically. For N=3, V_3 already has dimension 2, equal to the mean-zero space. Direct expansion gives E=3M, so D=dist\u00b2=0. Every stability coefficient then works vacuously; there is no meaningful finite optimal coefficient.\n\nNEAR EXTREMIZERS. For N\u22654, nonzero x, and \u03b5\u22650, E(x)/M(x)\u2264\u03bb\u2081+\u03b5 implies dist(x,V_N)/||x||\u2082\u2264min{1,sqrt(\u03b5/\u03b3)}. For every 0\u2264\u03b5\u2264\u03b3, choose x=v+w with M(w)/(M(v)+M(w))=\u03b5/\u03b3; these mixtures attain equality. Thus the coefficient is optimal even for arbitrarily small \u03b5. For \u03b5>\u03b3, the untruncated bound exceeds 1, while the sharp truncated bound is attained by a nonzero second harmonic. The zero vector satisfies the homogeneous inequality but has no defined Rayleigh quotient. Equivalently, with C_N=1/\u03bb\u2081,\nC_N E(x)\u2212M(x)\u2265(1+2cos\u03b8)dist(x,V_N)\u00b2.\nThus C_N E(x)/M(x)\u22641+\u03b4 implies normalized distance at most min{1,sqrt(\u03b4/(1+2cos\u03b8))}.\n\nMETHOD. Your objective is to audit the previously derived proofs for every N>=3, resolve any hidden boundary or equality degeneracies, and prepare a mathematically self-contained elementary theorem and proof suitable for consolidation with the separate DFT branch. Do not treat previous model-generated arguments as independently verified.

ASSUMPTIONS AND TARGET THEOREMS.
Fix N>=3 and a real cyclic vector x=(x_0,...,x_{N-1}) with x_N=x_0 and sum_j x_j=0. Write theta=2pi/N, M(x)=sum_j x_j^2, E(x)=sum_j(x_{j+1}-x_j)^2, lambda_1=4sin^2(pi/N), and D(x)=E(x)-lambda_1 M(x). Define V_N=span_R{(cos(theta j))_j,(sin(theta j))_j}. All norms are ordinary unnormalized Euclidean norms. The Round 1 theorem states that D(x)>=0, with equality exactly when x belongs to V_N. For N>=4, Round 2 claims the sharp strengthened inequality D(x)>=gamma_N dist(x,V_N)^2, where gamma_N=4sin^2(2pi/N)-4sin^2(pi/N)=lambda_1(1+2cos theta)>0. Stability equality is claimed exactly for x in V_N+W_N, with W_N the real second-harmonic space. For N=3, V_3 is the entire mean-zero space and D(x)=0 identically.

PRIOR ELEMENTARY CONSTRUCTION.
Set z=x-P_Nx, where P_N is the orthogonal projection onto V_N. For every r in {0,...,N-1}, define y_j^(r)=z_j-z_{r-j}, s_j^(r)=sin(theta(j-r/2)), and t_j^(r)=y_j^(r)/s_j^(r) where the denominator is nonzero, with t=0 at sine zeros. Prior rounds established sum_r M(y^(r))=2NM(z), sum_r D(y^(r))=2ND(z), and the factorization D(y^(r))=sum_j s_j^(r)s_{j+1}^(r)(t_{j+1}^(r)-t_j^(r))^2. Terms with negative weights vanish because the endpoints are exchanged by reflection; zero weights vanish trivially. Positive-weight terms occur on the positive and negative sine arcs and are paired by reflection.

On the positive sine arc, list consecutive angles h_1,...,h_m in (0,pi), separated by theta. Put s_i=sin h_i, phi_i=cos h_i, w_i=s_i^2, a_i=s_i s_{i+1} for 1<=i<m, and t_i=y_i/s_i. Define S=sum_{i=1}^m w_i t_i^2 and T=sum_{i=1}^{m-1}a_i(t_{i+1}-t_i)^2. Orthogonality to the first harmonic yields sum_i w_i t_i=0, while M(y)=2S and D(y)=2T. For m>=2, put F_i=sum_{k=1}^i w_k t_k, F_0=F_m=0, p_i=a_i(phi_i-phi_{i+1}) for 1<=i<m, p_0=p_m=0, and J=sum_{i=1}^{m-1}F_i^2/a_i. The Round 2 proof claims p_i>0, p_i-p_{i-1}=gamma_N w_i phi_i, and the two exact identities
K:=S-gamma_N J=sum_{i=1}^{m-2}[p_i p_{i+1}/w_{i+1}](F_i/p_i-F_{i+1}/p_{i+1})^2,
T-gamma_N S=sum_{i=1}^{m-1}a_i(t_{i+1}-t_i+gamma_N F_i/a_i)^2+gamma_N K.
For m=1 the weighted zero-mean constraint implies y=0. These certificates imply the sharp global stability theorem.

AUDIT TASK A — CYCLIC AND REFLECTION GEOMETRY.
Prove precisely the structure of positive and negative sine arcs for odd and even N. For odd N, determine the number of sine-zero vertices, sign-changing edges, and positive-sine vertices; repeat for even N with r even and r odd. Show explicitly that m=(N-1)/2 for odd N, while for even N, m=N/2-1 when r is even and m=N/2 when r is odd. Verify these formulas for N=3,4,5,6. Check all claims at the cyclic edge j=N-1 to j=0 using a consistent lifted index convention. Prove that every negative-weight edge has reflection-paired endpoints and equal ratios t, including both sign-changing boundaries. Establish that positive and negative arc contributions really coincide, with no missing or duplicated edges.

AUDIT TASK B — FLUX AND DUAL FACTORIZATION.
Independently rederive, by finite algebra and trigonometric addition identities, the relation p_i-p_{i-1}=gamma_N w_i phi_i at every i, including i=1 and i=m. At each omitted boundary edge, explicitly distinguish a neighboring sine zero from a half-step sign change and show why the boundary flux vanishes even when the product of neighboring sines is negative. Verify gamma_N=2cos theta-2cos(2theta)=lambda_1(1+2cos theta). Expand S in terms of F_i and verify every diagonal and mixed coefficient in the formula for K, including m=2 where the right-hand sum is empty. Recheck the finite summation-by-parts identity sum_i F_i(t_{i+1}-t_i)=-S and derive the full strengthened certificate without relying on a spectral theorem. Address all divisions by a_i, p_i, and w_i and explain why they are positive wherever used.

AUDIT TASK C — EQUALITY AND SHARPNESS.
Prove necessity and sufficiency of equality in the weighted certificate. Handle m=1 and m=2 separately; for m>=3 prove K=0 forces F_i/p_i constant. Verify that this yields t_i=kappa gamma_N cos h_i and that the remaining square terms vanish. Reconstruct y_j^(r) as a multiple of sin(2theta(j-r/2)), including at zero vertices and on reflected negative arcs. Use sum_r y_j^(r)=Nz_j to show that global equality implies z in W_N, and prove the converse directly using finite trigonometric sums and the second-harmonic recurrence. Explicitly classify W_4 as one-dimensional and W_N as two-dimensional for N>=5. Prove optimality by constructing a nonzero second harmonic perpendicular to V_N. Maintain a clear distinction between equality in the original Poincare inequality and equality in stability.

AUDIT TASK D — SMALL-N DEGENERACIES AND NORMALIZATION.
For N=3, verify E=3M, V_3 equals the mean-zero space, and no nontrivial complementary spectral gap or finite optimal stability coefficient exists. For N=4, verify D=2dist(x,V_4)^2 identically, including its direct expression 2(x_0+x_2)^2. For N=5, verify gamma_5=sqrt(5) and the exact stability identity for every zero-mean vector. For N=6, exhibit an additional higher mode and show why it gives strict stability inequality. Check the coefficient C_N=1/lambda_1 in M<=C_N E, the scaling under x to ax, and the equivalent strengthened formulation C_N E-M>=(gamma_N/lambda_1)dist(x,V_N)^2. Ensure no spurious factors of N, 2, or C_N enter any formula.

AUDIT TASK E — NEAR-EXTREMIZERS.
For N>=4 and x nonzero, verify rigorously that E(x)/M(x)<=lambda_1+epsilon implies dist(x,V_N)/||x||_2<=min{1,sqrt(epsilon/gamma_N)}. Derive the equivalent C_N-normalized version. Construct x=v+t w with v in V_N, w in W_N, v perpendicular to w, and calculate the exact Rayleigh quotient and normalized distance. Prove equality is achievable for every 0<=epsilon<=gamma_N and show why the truncated bound is optimal for epsilon>gamma_N. Distinguish arbitrary positive epsilon from asymptotic near-extremizers as epsilon tends to zero, and explain separately why the zero vector cannot be assigned a Rayleigh quotient.

METHODOLOGICAL AND REPORTING REQUIREMENTS.
Identify which parts of the final proof are genuinely elementary finite-sum arguments and which use trigonometric identities that are equivalent to individual eigenfunction calculations. Do not silently replace the weighted positivity argument by a complete Fourier diagonalization. If any prior claim is incorrect or insufficiently justified, state the precise obstruction and supply a correction if possible; an honest PARTIAL report is preferable to asserting an invalid proof. Present one concise but complete structured report, aiming for approximately 700 words while retaining all indispensable proof identities and exceptional cases. Include status, summary, findings, rigorous evidence, obstacles, recommended next steps, split_suggestion, and important_update as required by the research protocol. Do not use external sources or software, propose new children, or undertake an additional research round. Stop after submitting this mandatory Round 3 audit report. The parent coordinator will then assess whether the elementary branch is complete."}
